learning_outcomes.text: Recognize and understand the basic methodologies of linear algebra; geometry; differential geometry; differential and integral calculus; ordinary and partial differential equations; numerical methods; numerical algorithms; statistics, and optimization applied to engineering.
Solve, using mathematics and statistics, potential problems that may arise in engineering.
Recognize and understand the training needs that will be useful to successfully resolve new situations related to industrial engineering.
Propose creative solutions to satisfactorily respond to real needs and problems of society.
Develop professional texts and scientific-technical reports according to the conventions of the field of industrial technical engineering.
Adapt the organization of content and the use of verbal and non-verbal language to argue in diverse situations or before diverse audiences.
Apply the knowledge of industrial engineering in learning new methods and theories.
Show the advantages and opportunities of different solutions to the same problem critically and constructively.
Apply the principles and methods of quality.

syllabus_topics: Topic 1: First-Order Differential Equations. Introduction to techniques for solving linear and non-linear first-order differential equations.

Topic 2: Higher-Order Differential Equations and Systems of First-Order Differential Equations. Introduction to techniques for solving systems of differential equations based on Linear Algebra and their application to solving higher-order differential equations.
Topic 3: Introduction to Second-Order Two-Dimensional Partial Differential Equations. Classification. Two-dimensional heat, wave, and Laplace equations.

Topic 4: Differential Curves and Surfaces in the Plane and in Space. Differentiable curves in the plane and in space. Parametrized surfaces. First and second fundamental forms. Distinguishable curves on surfaces. Integration of scalar and vector functions over curves and surfaces.
Topic 5: Line and Surface Integrals - Vector fields in R^n, Green's, Stokes', and Gauss's Divergence Theorems.
teaching_methods: Problem/exercise solving in the ordinary classroom
assessment_rules: Two practical tests in the classroom, focused on exercises, problems, and questions related to the taught content, with a weight of 80% of the overall grade. Tasks and complementary exercises, which students can submit on established dates or perform in the classroom, with a weight of 20% of the overall assessment.
